teams.synopsis: The most wins in PFFL history, and Freiermuth/Likely already answered the Mark Andrews question.
teams.blurb: The biggest question surrounding this team a week ago was how it would handle the loss of <mark class="hl-player">Mark Andrews</mark>, and needless to say, <mark class="hl-player">Freiermuth</mark> and/or <mark class="hl-player">Likely</mark> answered that question and will give this team a good chance at winning in the playoffs. Ethan's team didn't put up the most points in Week 12, but with the most wins by a team in PFFL history, this team remained atop the rankings.

teams.synopsis: A locked-in top-two team, largely unchanged for a month, with a great playoff run set up.
teams.blurb: A locked-in top-two team in the league, Carmine's team hasn't changed much in the past month, and because of that he remains in this spot. He's set up for a great playoff run in 2023, but it'll be interesting to see how seeding plays out and who he ends up facing in the first round. Overall, a very good team that will continue to be very good.

teams.synopsis: A top team to close the season — tied for the best record in the AFC, seeding is the only question left.
teams.blurb: Staying in the top three this week, Brandon's team should be labeled a top team to conclude the season. A recent trade has given this team a top running back duo, and with no real holes in the lineup, Brandon will be a threat until proven otherwise. It'll be interesting to see how the final three weeks play out, because Brandon is currently tied for the best record in the AFC, but unless he finishes with a better record than Carmine, he won't get that 2nd seed (due to the big margin of points scored between the two).

teams.synopsis: Back into the top five — sub-100 only once all year, with 150+ upside at full health.
teams.blurb: I've decided to jump Charlie all the way back up into the top five, because he's scored over 100 points every week this year except one, and with a fully healthy team, this squad can put up 150+ any given week. A strong bench and a top starting lineup lock this team into a playoff berth, and I wouldn't be surprised if we're calling him the 2023 PFFL Champion in January.

teams.synopsis: Five straight weeks in the top five — Dak, ETN, and Kelce remain top-three at their positions.
teams.blurb: Even though Aidan falls down a spot this week, he remains in the top five for the 5th straight week. This team has surprised some people, but the top record with high-level production solidifies its position as a top team in the league. With <mark class="hl-player">Dak</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">ETN</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Kelce</mark> continuing to be top-three players at their respective positions, Aidan has a very good chance to make a deep playoff run, and the PFFL Championship is not out of the equation.

teams.synopsis: The unanimous best WR duo in the league — and still the only team in the PFFL without a single trade.
teams.blurb: With the unanimous best WR duo in the league, Cole has the potential to win any and every week. This is the only team in the PFFL this season that hasn't made a trade, but that hasn't mattered, because an excellent draft has this team averaging the 5th-most points per week. I've had this team as playoff-caliber since preseason, and even now he's set up to make the playoffs — but at least one more win is needed to comfortably say they're in.

teams.synopsis: Five straight wins finally snapped — sub-100 for the first time since Week 5.
teams.blurb: After five wins in a row, Anthony has finally lost. Week 11 marked the first time he scored less than 100 points since Week 5, an accomplishment only a handful of teams can say they've done. The recent trade for <mark class="hl-player">Jefferson</mark> was a big win for this team, and if he can hold onto his playoff status, the trade puts him in a position to win back-to-back PFFL Championships.

teams.synopsis: Two rough weeks in a row, but the roster and early-season form say this doesn't last.
teams.blurb: 'They need to study the downfall of Bay's team' — Baylen's team has had two awful weeks in a row, but I don't think it'll continue. The team lacks big names, but if the players can keep playing how they did to start the season, I have no doubt this team will make the playoffs. I don't know which group this team belongs to yet: the teams fighting for better seeds, or the teams fighting for a playoff spot. This week will show us how this team performs at full strength.

teams.synopsis: Two wins in a row sets up a real playoff push, with anyone's championship to win from there.
teams.blurb: Max has won two weeks in a row, which sets him up for a potential playoff push. His 2023 season has had its ups and downs, but with a somewhat weak rest-of-season schedule, I'd expect Max to have a chance to make the playoffs, and from there it's anyone's championship to win. I'm rooting for this team, but two more wins will most likely be needed.

teams.synopsis: Hit or miss across the roster — White, Montgomery, and Adams keep this team competitive with anyone.
teams.blurb: Deniz's team is a hard one to rank, because his players are so hit or miss. They don't really have a player who can win the matchup for them, but they do have guys like <mark class="hl-player">White</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Montgomery</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Adams</mark> who can consistently help Deniz compete with anyone in the league. I can see this team making its way into the 2023 PFFL Playoffs as the 8th seed, but at least two wins in the next three weeks will be needed to feel comfortable.

teams.synopsis: The biggest week of the season — a four-game losing streak on the line against another 4-7 team.
teams.blurb: This week might be the biggest week of Root's season — he takes on the only other 4-7 team, and a loss might signal the end of his season. As it sits right now, he's on a four-game losing streak, the longest active streak in the league. If he's able to snap the streak and win this week, then the playoffs are a possibility.

teams.synopsis: Not a threat to anyone, but a recent trade shows he's still playing to win now.
teams.blurb: Ryan isn't really a threat to anyone at this stage of the season, but he still has the opportunity to sneak into the playoffs and cause an upset. The most recent trade displays Ryan's willingness to do whatever it takes to win now, which may work out if he can get a win this week against another bottom team in the league. Look out for this team to make a playoff push, but don't fear them.

teams.synopsis: Eliminated with a 2-9 record — the Ben matchup is the biggest game of his season.
teams.blurb: Quin has also been officially eliminated from the playoffs this past week. He has a 2-9 record, tied for the worst in the league with Ben's team. This upcoming week marks the most important matchup of his season, because he plays Ben. The loser of this game will most likely have to do the punishment, so I'd expect Quin to go all in for the win. Better luck in 2024!

teams.synopsis: Mathematically eliminated — this week against Quin is really about who avoids the punishment.
teams.blurb: Officially mathematically eliminated from the playoffs, Ben's team had a shaky 2023 season. It's unfortunate that players like <mark class="hl-player">Jones</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Kupp</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Watson</mark> didn't have the seasons Ben hoped for, but that's part of the game. This week is an extremely important matchup against Quin, which may decide who does the punishment.
